blocks.text:
I'm checking distances from the calcium atom to nearby oxygen and nitrogen atoms in surrounding residues, and ASN738's OD1 looks close enough at about 2.35 Å to be a coordinating atom.

Continuing the search, ASN757 OD1 comes out to roughly 2.31 Å and VAL736's carbonyl oxygen at about 2.33 Å, both plausible coordinators, while most other nearby backbone and side-chain atoms are too distant to count.

Checking the remaining candidates - ASP737, GLY752, SER753, LEU739, ASP760 - none fall within a reasonable coordination distance. So it looks like the coordinating set is V736, N738, and N757, though a typical calcium site often has more ligands, so there may be a water molecule filling out the coordination sphere.

Continuing to scan the backbone atoms of residues 735-738 against the pocket bounds, checking ALA735 N/CA/C/O, VAL736 N and O, ASP737 N, and now ASN738 N—most fall outside the distance cutoff, confirming VAL736 O as the only additional close contact so far.
